btr.$note: 43 attachment(s) are listed for this Party's BTR1. 2 of 8 components are evidenced by an attachment name; the rest are unread, not missing. Adaptation and Article 6 are chapters inside the report rather than separate attachments, so no filename can evidence them and both stay unknown for every Party. Submission dates are not in this listing.

vulnerability.$note: From the 2026 bulk release, latest available year. ND-GAIN restates earlier years between releases (Cambodia 2021 read 40.1 in the edition cited by data/khm.json and 40.665 here); rank is not in the bulk file.

series.$note: series.observed holds several sources and must not be read as one curve. DS-35: All greenhouse gases including land-use change, GWP100 (OWID, from Climate Watch / PIK), from 1990. DS-02: Asset-level observed emissions, CO₂e GWP100 (Climate TRACE); land use accounted differently from OWID, 2015-2025. DS-40: Total GHG emissions including LULUCF/LUCF exactly as the Party submitted them to the UNFCCC, on that Party’s own reporting guidelines and GWP set (UNFCCC Data Interface, snapshot of 2024-07-05). Non-Annex I Parties report only the years their national communications cover, and the figure is negative where reported removals exceed reported emissions. Points from an NDC document are that document's own inventory basis. The same year can appear more than once with different values; R3 keeps them side by side and never averages them.

derived.$reason: 35 observed years are loaded, but no NDC target emissions figure has been parsed, so there is nothing to measure the trend against.

country_profile.$note: Population is World Bank SP.POP.TOTL for the latest year published in the 2015–2025 window. Income group is the World Bank's own classification, not a UNFCCC one.

ndc_assessment.vintage: First (I)NDC round, as assessed by WRI CAIT (2016). Not the latest submission.
ndc_assessment.summary: The United States intends to achieve an economy-wide target of reducing its greenhouse gas emissions by 26%-28% below its 2005 level in 2025 and to make best efforts to reduce its emissions by 28%.
ndc_assessment.ghg_target: 26% to 28% reduction in GHG emission by 2025 compared to 2005 and to make best efforts to reduce its emissions by 28%
ndc_assessment.gases: CO2, CH4, N2O, HFCs, PFCs, SF6, NF3
ndc_assessment.sectors: The U.S. target covers all IPCC sectors.
ndc_assessment.$note: Third-party assessment of the first (I)NDC round. It is not merged into ndc.*, is not used by derive(), and does not appear on the dial as a target.

ndc_document.$reason: no sentence in this document states an economy-wide percentage reduction against a base year or a business-as-usual projection.
ndc_document.$note: Read by DS-06-NDC from the First NDC as mirrored by openclimatedata; unfccc.int itself refuses this engine's requests. Nothing was accepted from this document.

Total GHG emissions including LULUCF/LUCF exactly as the Party submitted them to the UNFCCC, on that Party’s own reporting guidelines and GWP set (UNFCCC Data Interface, snapshot of 2024-07-05). emissions_profile.$note: Headline totals are OWID only. OWID's CO₂ sub-totals are fossil/industrial CO₂ by fuel, not a full sectoral GHG breakdown, and do not sum to total_mtco2e. DS-05's rows are non-CO₂ gases only and are not comparable with the others; that is also why DS-05 is absent from series.observed, where a shorter curve would read as a disagreement rather than a difference of scope. by_source carries each source whole.

verdict.text: The UNFCCC registry holds no active NDC for this Party: the registry lists 3 submission(s) for this Party and none of them is active. 78 observed values are loaded from DS-02 (11), DS-35 (35), DS-40 (32). For 2024 the sources disagree: DS-02 6941.4 MtCO₂e, DS-35 6054.3 MtCO₂e. They are on different inventory scopes and the engine does not reconcile them. No implementation gap is reported: 35 observed years are loaded, but no NDC target emissions figure has been parsed, so there is nothing to measure the trend against. It submitted BTR1. 2 of 8 components have been confirmed in the document; the rest are unparsed, which is not a finding against the country. ND-GAIN scores it 65.7 for 2024. In the first NDC round, WRI's CAIT assessment recorded: 26% to 28% reduction in GHG emission by 2025 compared to 2005 and to make best efforts to reduce its emissions by 28% It was classed unconditional. That is a 2016 assessment of an earlier submission, not the target above. Projected warming for 2080-2099 against 1995-2014 ranges from +1.6°C under SSP1-2.6 to +5.38°C under SSP5-8.5. These are model runs, not observations.
